title: Brain-Focused Research on Antiretrovirals and Methamphetamine (Brain-FRAMe)
text:
PUBLIC HEALTH STATEMENT
People who use methamphetamine are at high risk for HIV infection, and continuing use of methamphetamine
substantially increases their risk for medical, neurological, and mental health disorders. These conditions make
it difficult for people with HIV who use methamphetamine to adhere to medications and remain in medical care.
The Brain-FRAMe program aims to build on recent advances to control HIV and reduce methamphetamine use
and the risk of transmitting HIV to others, to expand knowledge about the biological mechanisms that are
associated with changes in brain health, and provide a blueprint for improving treatment of people with HIV and
methamphetamine addiction to advance the goals of ending the HIV epidemic.

title: Engineered extracellular vesicles derived from mesenchymal stem cells for the treatment of type 1 diabetes
text:
Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is an autoimmune disease wherein a loss in immune tolerance leads to the
progressive destruction of insulin-producing β cells, resulting in hyperglycemia and complications, but there is
no cure for T1D. This proposal will investigate whether extracellular vesicles (EVs) produced by mesenchymal
stem cells (MSCs) can induce immune tolerance, thereby ablating T1D-associated autoimmunity. The success
of the proposed research will provide essential insights and valuable information for the rational design of EV-
based interventions, ultimately leading to the development of novel, safe and clinically feasible cell-free therapy
using MSC-derived EVs for T1D treatment.

title: Center for Cancer Immunology and Immunotherapy (CCII)
text: Decades of research have demonstrated that the immune system can eradicate cancer cells but only if immune evasion mechanisms, such as immune checkpoint proteins, can be overcome. Multiple new immunotherapeutic approaches have recently been developed that can induce durable remissions in patients with advanced cancers – unfortunately, most patients still succumb to their cancers. The goal of this COBRE Phase 2 application is to enhance the successful Center for Cancer Immunology & Immunotherapy that focuses on understanding immune escape mechanisms, developing new approaches to activate and reinvigorate anticancer immunity, training promising junior cancer immunologists, and improving the research infrastructure at the University of Louisville.

title: Electronic Cigarettes as a Harm Reduction Strategy Among People with Opioid Use Disorder on Buprenorphine
text:
This K01 proposal aims to investigate the impact of e-cigarette (EC) flavors and usage patterns on achieving
harm reduction milestones. Utilizing the RE-AIM Framework, we will identify barriers and facilitators to
implementing and maintaining the EC protocol in both rural and urban settings. The findings will offer preliminary
evidence of the harm reduction potential of ECs and provide strategies for implementing and sustaining EC-
based harm reduction protocols. If successful and sustainable, these protocols may ultimately reduce tobacco-
related morbidity and mortality among individuals with opioid use disorder on buprenorphine.

title: Impact of opioid use disorder on mitochondrial dysfunction among antiretroviral therapy-receiving aging people with HIV.
text:
The combination of HIV, aging and opioid addiction may aggravate proinflammatory immune response
triggered by mitochondrial dysfunction in immune cells, and could be extremely detrimental for the
health outcomes of long-term antiretroviral therapy receiving older people with HIV (PWH), who also
have opioid use disorder (OUD). Therefore, the extent of mitochondrial dysfunction in various immune
cell subsets needs to be assessed in this vulnerable group of people using focused and high throughput
experiments. This proposal aims to advance foundational knowledge about the role of mitochondria in
the age-related altered immune cell function in older PWH with OUD, which could be leveraged to
develop targeted therapies and improve outcomes in people aging with HIV, opioid use and addiction.

title: Speckle x-ray imaging: detecting early changes in lung microstructure
text:
Public Health Relevance.
The number of cancer survivors is steadily increasing; for example, in 2019 an estimated 16.9 million individuals
in the United States alone were considered cancer survivors. With this positive upward trend in survivorship, the
long-term lung toxicity of radiation therapy gains importance. To address this critical need, we propose a simple,
sensitive, and low-dose imaging tool that utilizes a single x-ray projection to detect the early onset of radiation-
induced lung fibrosis.

title: Understanding how structural mutations and individual RNA isoforms are involved in human health and disease
text:
There are many subtleties in human health and disease that remain unexplained. In our efforts
to help personalize medicine, we seek to better understand how individual RNA isoforms affect
human health disease by helping characterize them and their roles in human health and
disease.

title: Exploring the neural architecture of psychedelic experience with high-density electrophysiology
text:
While the clinical benefits of psychedelics for neuropsychiatric disorders like depression and PTSD are
increasingly well-documented, we lack a brain-wide, systems-level view of how a single treatment leads to lasting
therapeutic effects. This project is designed to fill that gap—I will generate and analyze a comprehensive, high-
density electrophysiology dataset to map the brain-wide effects of psilocybin over time in behaving animals. This
resource will not only improve our fundamental understanding of psychedelic action but will also create an
invaluable platform for investigating neural plasticity, developing novel therapeutics, and characterizing the
electrophysiological signatures of the depressed brain.

title: T Cells and IL-9 Signaling at the Maternal-Fetal Interface in Preterm Labor and Birth
text:
Preterm birth is the leading cause of neonatal death worldwide, and those who survive commonly have long-
term negative health consequences. The work proposed here on immune cells at the maternal-fetal interface
may lead to new treatments to prevent preterm birth and improve outcomes for preterm infants.

title: Next Generation Sequencing Core
text:
The Next Generation Sequencing core (NGSC) is responsible for all high-throughput sequencing and
bioinformatics activities required for DNA, RNA and ChIP-sequencing. All activities including library
preparations will be done at the NGSC and will be done closely connected with the ACC NGS Core facility
supported by the NCI Abramson Cancer Center.

title: Regulation of Tumor Immunogenicity in Glioblastoma
text:
Glioblastoma (GBM) is an incurable disease with current treatment including surgery, chemotherapy, and
radiation. Immunotherapy has thus far failed in clinical trials for GBM. Our studies provide a novel therapeutics
target, PP2A, in glioma cells to enhance GBM immunogenicity and sensitivity to immunotherapy.

title: Computational Modeling and Analysis Core
text:
Computational Modeling and Analysis (CMA) Core
The Computational Modeling and Analysis Core will provide state-of-the-art AI and deep learning frameworks
as well as advanced statistical design and analysis support for projects focused on the neurosciences. These
services will meet the critical recognized need for computational resources to increase scientific rigor and
leverage modern tools and statistical learning for big data.

title: Biomarker Core - Cleveland ADRC
text: The mission of the Cleveland Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center (CADRC) Biomarker Core (BC) is to support Alzheimer's disease (AD) and AD-related dementia (ADRD) research by collecting, storing, tracking, sharing, and analyzing biospecimens and associated clinical and biomarker data. The BC aims to advance deep phenotyping and novel biomarker discovery to support investigating factors related to disease risk and progression through biomarker profiling of CADRC cohorts. Cohorts include participants with distinct clinical phenotypes such as 1) atypical AD (multiple cortical variants of AD), 2) dementia with Lewy-Bodies (DLB), 3) mixed dementia (e.g. AD+DLB), 4) Cognitively Normal (CN) amyloid positive, preclinical-AD, 5) amnestic mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and typical AD dementia stages confirmed by biofluid biomarkers of AD and α- Synuclein real-time quaking-induced conversion (RT-QuIC) seed amplification assays (SAA) and neuroimaging biomarkers of MRI, amyloid and tau PET. Deep molecular phenotyping through BC analysis will include core AD biomarkers and in addition support novel biomarker discovery with longitudinally collected biofluids and case- matched autopsy brain tissue, when available. The BC builds on established infrastructure and scientific strengths in neurodegenerative disease, biobanking, novel biomarker discovery, and assay development, and established integrated biospecimen collection and BC workflows between Case Western Reserve University, Cleveland Clinic Foundation, University Hospitals, and the Veterans Affairs Northeast Ohio Health Care System. Aims of the BC are to 1) Facilitate research with biobanking and distribution of biospecimens and corresponding data with cross-core collaboration, 2) Support comprehensive AD/ADRD biomarker profiling and discovery with biofluid specimens, 3) Enable studies of longitudinal changes in biofluid biomarkers, the accumulation of misfolded proteins, and support studies on rate of progression, and 4) Sustain mentorship activities in biomarker research and foster collaborations with junior and established investigators to encourage project innovation. Biomarker data linked to relevant clinical data in accordance with goals of the National Alzheimer's Project Act are shared with the scientific community including the National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center. Our established BC team leverages expertise in AD/ADRD biomarker evaluation, seed amplification assays, proteomics platforms, biobanking and bioinformatics to provide comprehensively profiled biospecimens for AD/ADRD research and biomarker discovery.

title: Multi-scale modulation of organ adaptation
text:
During a human’s lifetime, organs modulate their functions and forms in response to changing physiological
needs and external stimuli to reach their best possible performance levels. The epigenetic mechanism
responsible for this adaptation is unknown. We use the avian integument model to study this process.

title: Discovery Proteomics Core
text: The Discovery Proteomics Core (DPC) uses cutting edge and robust sample preparation, state-of-the-art proteomic and complementary biophysical, and lipidomics technologies to analyze adaptive changes in neuronal signal transduction mechanisms that occur in response to drugs of abuse. Aim 1 uses Data Dependent Acquisition (DDA) and Data-Independent Acquisition (DIA) to identify proteins whose expression or posttranslational modifications (PTMs) are altered in cell-based systems, tissue from discrete brain regions, single cell types and their organelles isolated with LCM, FACS, FANS or single cell dispensing. We will continue to build project specific spectral libraries to support DIA assays as well as implement library-free searches. Aim 2 uses immunological and chemical approaches to enrich for peptides and proteins containing PTMs to facilitate their identification. In collaboration with TPC, the DPC will integrate PTM analyses into DIA, including use of FAIMS based data acquisition for glycosylation and “Middle-down” analyses, and use Parallel Reaction Monitoring by the TPC to validate differentially expressed proteins and PTMs. Aim 3 uses “Middle- down” analyses to identify the multiple PTMs that occur in individual proteoforms such as the combinatorial epigenetic changes in histone modification. In Aim 4 we will use new tools and databases to improve analysis and interpretation of large scale, quantitative MS/proteomics data sets. To improve peptide identification from searching databases with MS/MS spectra, we will implement a CHIMERYS search mechanism for DDA and DIA data; and we will collaborate with the Biostatistics and Bioinformatics Core to enable MS/MS searches of RNA-sequencing-predicted proteomes. In Aim 5 we will purify recombinant proteins and exosomes from plasma or cell culture media for our investigators and use Nanoparticle Tracking Analysis, Dynamic Light Scattering, and Asymmetric Flow Field-Flow-Fractionation coupled with Multiangle Static Light Scattering to characterize size distribution and to fractionate the purified exosomes. In Aim 6 we will monitor localization and metabolism of phosphoinositide lipids, a major class of signaling lipids, in brain circuits involved in addiction and provide methodology for studying the role of intracellular protein-mediated lipid transport in the control of these circuits. In Aim 7, we will provide training in experimental design, sample preparation, and use of software for analysis and interpretation of MS data, biophysical, and phosphoinositide analyses. The DPC will ensure that the Center's research is supported by the most advanced instrumentation and biotechnologies. By taking a holistic approach the DPC will provide Center investigators with the broad range of tools and training needed to identify, and then to understand why certain proteins and their PTMs and phosphoinositide effectors are differentially expressed following exposure to drugs of abuse.

title: SBIR: In vivo engineering of multifaceted B7H3.CAR-T cells for cellular immunotherapy of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
text:
T cells reprogrammed to display chimeric antigen receptors (CARs) represent a promising therapeutic modality
for a number of cancers, but currently suffer from high costs and modest efficacy against solid tumors. In this
proposal, we seek to directly reprogram T-cells that are circulating in the blood to display CAR against the B7-
H3 antigen highly overexpressed on pancreatic cancers, and evaluate the effectiveness of such CAR-T cells
against pancreatic cancer in suitable mouse models. If successful, this work will advance a potentially more
efficacious and cost-effective treatment for pancreatic cancer.

title: Models and Gene Therapies for AAT Deficiency-Core B
text: Project Summary - Core B To have successful therapies for Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency it is necessary to have animal models that recapitulate the phenotypes see in human patients to test therapeutics, including gene therapy and genome editing approaches, and develop clinically relevant therapeutic benchmarks to ascertain the success of those therapies. To achieve this, we are working with the primary investigators (PIs) of Project 1 (Flotte), Project 2 (Wang), and Project 3 (Xue) to breed, manage, dose, and analyze mouse and ferret AATD models to answer their respective research questions. We have in our colony AAT-Null-PiZ ferrets, AAT-Null mice, AAT-Null-PiZ mice, and wild-type (C57Bl6) mice that we will breed and manage in order to supply animals to the Projects as needed. Core B will also provide expertise in respiratory physiology measurements, animal handling, gene therapy dosing, in vivo sample collection, and necropsy to provide post-mortem sample collection to all of the Projects. In addition to the maintenance of mouse and ferret models for use in Projects 1, 2, and 3, we will also work with Projects 1 and 3 to characterize the pulmonary phenotype responses to gene therapy and genome editing. The core will provide expertise in murine and ferret pulmonary function testing, bronchoalveolar lavage, and facilitation of vector dosing as needed.

title: Effects of cannabidiol (CBD) on synaptic excitatory and inhibitory balance
text:
Dravet syndrome (DS) is a developmental epileptic encephalopathy that is considered a severe form of epilepsy
involving treatment-resistant seizures. In 2018, the FDA approved Epidiolex (CBD) for the treatment of seizures
associated with DS ≥ 2 years of age; yet, CBD’s mechanism of action for managing seizures remains largely
unknown. An enhanced understanding of neurobiological mechanisms that mediate the anticonvulsant effects
of CBD in DS could have substantial implications for improving the outcomes of children with DS.

title: Role of serum advanced glycation end-products in altering tendon properties with diabetes
text:
This project seeks to understand the role of serum advanced glycation end-products in the high frequency of
tendon injury and impaired function in millions of Americans with diabetes. This critical project will use genetic
mouse models and the study of people with diabetes to delineate the role of serum advanced glycation end-
products in tendon injury and impaired function. With a long-term goal of developing new prevention and
treatment strategies, this research will identify novel serum factors that drive tendon injury and impaired tendon
function in the growing number of individuals with diabetes.

title: Occupational Safety and Ergonomics Training Program
text:
The COVID-19 pandemic underscored the critical role of ergonomics and human factors in emergency
management and occupational safety, while amplifying job insecurity, work-family imbalances, and
psychosocial stressors, emphasizing the need for skilled professionals. Furthermore, the rapid integration of
artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, and automation into workplaces has introduced emerging risks, further
highlighting the necessity of training a new generation of experts. These professionals must understand
cutting-edge technologies, evaluate their impacts, and apply critical thinking to design and implement systems
that integrate humans, machines, and technology safely and effectively.
